To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have designed and developed a web-based protein structure search system that can simultaneously support two comparison methods, and we have evaluated the system by conducting experiments on the PDB database.
a new web server is developed that can efficiently search for global and local structural similarity in the Protein Data Bank.
ProteinDBS is a web server providing efficient and accurate global and local structural comparison of proteins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following aspects.
the development of efficient and accurate algorithms for structural comparison of proteins and their applications.

the following issues: (1) the design of efficient algorithms for protein structure comparison, (2) the development of scalable indexing methods for large-scale databases, (3) the implementation of a web server to facilitate the use of our system and (4) the evaluation of the performance of our system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ProteinDBS v.2 is a very powerful and efficient web server for global as well as local protein structure searches.
ProteinDBS v.2.0 is an excellent tool for protein structure comparison and search.
ProteinDBS v. 2.0 provides a very useful tool for the analysis of protein structures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ProteinDBS v1.0 has been replaced by ProteinDBS v3.0, which is a new web server with more features and better performance.
we have developed a fast and accurate search tool for global-to-global and global-to-local comparisons.
we are able to search the PDB database for global or local similarity in seconds, while preserving high precision.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of advanced indexing techniques and feature extraction algorithms can achieve a high-running efficiency with reasonably high precision in structural comparison.
we can use a database of 152,959 protein chains and search for the best match to a given query structure in a few seconds.
